title: Understanding Data Movement Patterns in HPC: A NERSC Case Study
problem: Data movement patterns in HPC have shifted and current infrastructure cannot efficiently handle competing transfers, resulting in up to 30% throughput degradation for individual flows.
motivation: Scientific experiments produce unprecedented data volumes requiring efficient data movement for successful workflow execution and reducing time to scientific results.
method: The authors analyzed three years of network traffic data from NERSC to identify data movement trends and detect bottlenecks. They characterized how patterns evolved over time and quantified the performance impact of competing transfers on existing infrastructure.
key_novelty: Comprehensive three-year longitudinal analysis of NERSC network traffic revealing shifted data movement patterns and quantifying infrastructure limitations under competing transfer loads.
contributions: Three-year longitudinal analysis of NERSC network traffic identifying critical data movement trends
Quantification of 30% throughput degradation caused by competing transfers
Design recommendations for data movement management in future integrated research infrastructures
End-to-end infrastructure paradigm integrating compute, network, and storage across facilities

metrics.other: 30% throughput degradation, transfer latency reduction, time to scientific results

limitations: Study limited to NERSC facility; future infrastructure recommendations not evaluated against implemented alternatives.
